questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was a great man with a high level of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **intellect**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"intellect"** means the faculty of reasoning and understanding objectively, especially with regard to abstract matters. (बुद्धि)

 
 
• **Example: **His intellect was evident in the way he solved complex problems effortlessly.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was a great man with a high level of **'intellect'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **intellect**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Intelligent humour** (बुद्धिमान हास्य): Humour that is clever and thought-provoking.

 
 
• **Example:** His intelligent humour always made people laugh and think at the same time.
 
 
 
• **Wise boredom** (समझदार ऊब): A state of being bored but having the wisdom to understand it.
 
 
• **Example: **During the long lecture, he experienced wise boredom, knowing it was important to stay attentive.
 
 
 
• **Clever fatigue** (चतुर थकान): A state of tiredness that is cleverly managed.
 
 
• **Example:** Despite his clever fatigue, he managed to complete all his tasks efficiently.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Ramesh __is owning__ a beautiful house in Noida.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the verb 'is owning' is incorrect.
 
• The verb **'own'** is a **stative verb** and is not usually used in continuous forms.
 
• Therefore, the simple present form of the verb 'owns' should be used in place of the present continuous form 'is owning'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *Ramesh **owns** a beautiful house in Noida*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Stative verbs describe a state rather than an action. They are not usually used in continuous (progressive) tenses.
 
 
• **Example:** *I **know** the answer (not 'am knowing')*.
 
• **Example:** *She **loves** chocolate (not 'is loving')*.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

When Nisha will have finished her task?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'When Nisha will' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the use of "will" after "when" is incorrect. The correct form should be "When Nisha has finished".
 
• In English grammar, when a sentence starts with "when", "if", or other similar conjunctions, the future tense is not used directly after them.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be "When Nisha has finished her task?".

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *When Nisha has finished her task?*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the **sentence starts with conjunctions like "when", "if", etc.**, the future tense is not used directly after them.

 
 
• For instance, instead of saying "When she will come", we should say "When she comes".

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He __push the bushes__ aside and went a little farther.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. pushed the bushes .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the verb form 'push' is incorrect.
 
• The subject **'He'** is **singular**, so the verb should be in the past tense (to maintain parallelism with** 'went'**, which is also in the past tense) to match the subject.
 
• The correct verb form here is 'pushed' to indicate an action completed in the past.
 
• Therefore, the correct substitution is 'pushed the bushes'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *He pushed the bushes aside and went a little farther*.
